label: The Wasserstein Distances
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 93 through 112 and turns the optimal transport cost into a genuine distance between probability measures. Frame the whole hour around one promise: choosing the cost to be a power of the ground distance produces a metric whose scale reads off both geometry and moments.

label: From Transport Cost to Distance
notes: Recall that the Kantorovich problem minimizes expected cost over couplings sharing the prescribed marginals. Stress that nothing yet makes the optimal value symmetric or additive; the Wasserstein construction is exactly the choice of cost that forces those metric properties to hold.

label: Definition of W_p
notes: Give the definition slowly. The cost is the ground distance raised to power p, we minimize its integral over couplings, then take a p-th root to restore the right units. Emphasize that the root is what makes W_p scale like a length rather than like an energy.

label: The Space P_p(X)
notes: Explain why we must restrict the universe of measures. Without a finite p-th moment the infimum can be infinite, so W_p lives on the set of measures whose p-th moment against a base point converges. Note that finiteness is independent of which base point we pick.

label: Symmetry and Separation
notes: Walk through the easy metric axioms. Symmetry comes from swapping the two coordinates of a coupling, and nonnegativity is immediate. The separation axiom uses that the diagonal coupling costs zero only when the two measures coincide, so distance zero forces equality.

label: Gluing Couplings
notes: Introduce the gluing lemma as the engine of the triangle inequality. Given a coupling of the first pair and a coupling of the second sharing the middle marginal, disintegrate and recombine to build a single measure on the triple whose two outer marginals are the ones we need.

label: The Triangle Inequality
notes: Now cash in the gluing. Project the three-fold measure to the outer pair, bound the ground distance by the path through the middle, and apply the Minkowski inequality in L-p. The result is W_p of the outer pair at most the sum of the two leg distances.

label: The Topology of W_p
notes: State the convergence theorem carefully. Convergence in W_p is equivalent to weak convergence together with convergence of p-th moments, equivalently convergence of integrals of every continuous function growing no faster than the p-th power. This is strictly stronger than plain weak convergence.

label: Ordering: W_p <= W_q
notes: Use Jensen or Holder on the coupling to compare orders. Because the p-th root of an average is monotone in p, a smaller exponent yields a smaller or equal distance. Larger p weighs long-range mass transport more heavily and therefore metrizes a finer, stronger topology.

label: Polish Space Structure
notes: Summarize the structural payoff. When the ground space is complete and separable, so is the metric space of measures with finite p-th moment under W_p. Completeness lets Cauchy sequences converge, and separability supplies a countable dense set of finitely supported measures.

label: Computational Reading: W1 versus W2
notes: Tie back to the notebook lab. Solving the finite Kantorovich linear program on the same two measures and reading off W1 and W2 side by side shows how raising p re-penalizes a single far move, and a third measure numerically confirms the triangle inequality the proof guaranteed.

label: Synthesis and Outlook
notes: Close by collecting the four claims: W_p is a metric, P_p is Polish, the topology is weak convergence plus moments, and orders are nested. Preview that this distance becomes the stage on which displacement interpolation, geodesics, and curvature are built in later chapters.
